## News themes

- The 10-year gilt yield stood at 5.3337% on 21 Oct, within a 4.8802%–5.4292% range since late July, and up from 4.9715% at the start of the period (Bank of England Database).

## What it means for our portfolio
- **City Core assets** (108 Cannon Street, 138 Cheapside, 16 Old Bailey): prime rent at £100 psf [F57] strengthens re-gear and reversion potential, though gilts near 5.33% and April's rates rise [D54#0] temper value gains. - **Regent Quarter** (King's Cross): our leasing note expects AI and life-science tenants to pre-let new Grade A space around King's Cross and Euston [D196#3]; OpenAI's lease already anchors the estate per portfolio records.

## Coming up
- Higher business-rates multipliers apply from next April [D54#0].
- Nothing else dated in this week's news.

**We declined Example House on 14 March 2024.** The proposal was to buy the 45,000 sq ft City Core office from Example Office Holdings Limited for £68m [D194#1], and the investment committee turned it down [D194#2]. Note that this is a mock internal document, written for a proof of concept, not a real Nan Fung record [D194#0].

**The reasons given were:**
- The asking price was above our replacement-cost estimate of about £1,250 per sq ft [D194#3]
- The building is rated EPC F, and reaching EPC B would cost about £11m [D194#3]
- The main tenant, paying 62% of the rent, leaves in 2026 [D194#3]

Two of those reasons map directly onto our hard rules: no purchase rated below EPC C without a costed plan to reach EPC B before 2031, and no single-let building with under three years left on its lease unless priced as empty [D195#3] (also a mock example).

**Worth knowing now:** Example Office Holdings Limited — the seller — went into administration on or around 21 October 2026, according to a Gazette-style notice [D186#0]. The notice says the company bought the 45,000 sq ft City building in 2018 with a five-year bank loan [D186#0], so the asset may come back to market via the administrators.

I found no record of this asset in the opportunity-card decisions, so the IC note above is the only decision trail we hold.
